To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

common genetic variation in the CHGB locus influences catecholamine storage and secretion, autonomic control of BP, and resting BP in the population; the effects on CHGB gene expression, catecholamine release, and BP are sexually dimorphic; and the CHGB locus is an important new locus for probing the genetic basis of autonomic control of cardiovascular function in the population.

common genetic variation at the human CHGB locus, most prominently in the proximal CHGB promoter, influences CHBG expression and later catecho-lamine secretion, autono-mic stability of circulation, and resting/basal blood pressure in the population, in a sex-dependent manner.
common variation at the CHBG locus is associated with variation in catecholamine release, autonomic stability, and resting BP, and that this variation is sex dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of autonomic control of the cardiovascular system and blood pressure (BP).
the role of genetic variation in autonomic control of the circulation.
the role of catecholamine (CA) storage vesicles in the regulation of blood pressure (BP).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

common variation in the CHGB gene is associated with variation in CHGB expression in vivo, which is associated with variation (in both men and women) in catecholamine release in vivo, which in turn is associated with variation of BP in vivo.
the common genetic variants at the CHGB gene locus influence CHGB expression, catecholamine storage and secretion, and autonomic function, eventuating in the heritable population BP phenotype.

the CHGB gene, which is expressed exclusively in catecholamine-secreting cells, plays a role in the control of BP in the population, that the CHGB locus is a genetic determinant of CHGB expression and catecholaminergic function, and that the CHGB promoter is a locus that contributes to BP variability in the population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CHGB gene is a major determinant of the early autonomic control of BP in the population and that this is mediated through the proximal promoter.

common genetic variation in the proximal CHGB promoter is a predictor of basal CHGB secretion in the population, that this is a heritable trait, and that the same promoter variant is a predictor of the BP response to environmental stimuli in the population.
common variation at the CHB locus is a major contributor to the heritable variation in autonomic control of blood pressure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CHGB is a key regulator of catecholamine storage in the adrenal medulla and sympathetic neurons.
CHGB variation is an important determinant of autonomic control of BP and that this is an important new locus in human autonomic function.
the CHGB gene is a novel regulator of BP in humans and a new target for the treatment of hypertension.
